St John of God Bunbury Hospital is seeking an experienced and motivated Deputy Combined Facilities Manager to join our team at the South West Health Campus. In this key leadership role, you will support the management and maintenance of the site's assets and infrastructure, ensuring they remain safe, reliable, and fit for purpose.

Working closely with the Combined Facilities Manager, you will help ensure all facilities and essential services meet operational requirements, regulatory standards, and licensing obligations. You will drive best-practice asset management strategies, optimise performance and reliability, and support the delivery of cost-effective facilities services that contribute to exceptional patient care and hospital operations.

The role is offered on a Permanent Full-Time basis, working 76 hours per fortnight.

The Position:

Demonstrate Lead the maintenance and reliability of critical hospital infrastructure and essential services, ensuring assets are safe, compliant, and operational through risk-based preventative maintenance and best-practice asset management.

Coordinate maintenance activities, contractors, and compliance requirements, including job planning, resource management, permit administration, documentation control, CMMS (MEX) management, and the resolution of plant and system breakdowns.

Monitor and optimise critical building services and asset performance, including HVAC, water, air quality, and medical gas systems, through effective use of the BMS and CMMS, KPI reporting, preventative maintenance, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Drive maintenance planning, compliance, and operational excellence by managing asset data, service contracts, shutdowns, training, documentation, audits, and reliability improvement programs to ensure safe, efficient, and compliant hospital operations

Support team leadership and operational planning by facilitating regular team meetings and assisting with budget development, capital works planning, and asset replacement strategies.

Ensure compliance and governance standards are met through adherence to organisational policies, regulatory requirements, licensing obligations, and workplace health, safety, and fire regulations.

The successful candidate will hold a relevant trade qualification and bring proven experience in a similar facilities or engineering role. They will possess extensive knowledge of building codes, Australian Standards, and hospital engineering services, including HVAC, boilers, steam systems, sterilisation processes, and a broad understanding of mechanical, plumbing, refrigeration, electrical, and building services trades. Experience using a Computerised Maintenance Management System (CMMS) and preparing maintenance documentation and reports is essential.

You will be a strong communicator with the ability to build effective stakeholder relationships and reliable professional networks. Demonstrated problem-solving skills, the ability to analyse and resolve complex technical issues, and a commitment to high-quality service delivery are essential.

The role requires participation in an after-hours on-call roster and the ability to obtain nomination on the hospital's in-house Electrical Licence if not already held.

What you'll be doing
 

The Fellow will be assigned to the Medical Oncology Department for the specified term of 1 year and will undertake specific tasks and responsibilities both clinically in Phase 1 as well as in research in Head and Neck Carcinoma with specific emphasis on immunotherapeutics. 

The Phase 1 Medical Oncology Fellow will have completed or be completing the Royal Australasian College of Physicians (RACP) training program or Royal College of Physicians (MRCP) program. They will be located within The Kinghorn Cancer Centre, St Vincent's Hospital and Garvan Institute as needed. The Fellow will be assigned to the Medical Oncology Department for the specified term of 1 year and will undertake specific tasks and responsibilities both clinically as well as in research in Phase 1 Medical Oncology with specific emphasis on immunotherapeutics. The Fellow will work as part of a multidisciplinary team and supervise junior medical officers (JMOs), research and medical students. It is also expected that the Fellow participates in the clinical meetings and teaching and be subject to training and performance reviews. Initiative to undertake a higher degree in combination with this work eg PhD, MD is encouraged. Routine clinical service responsibilities will be appropriate to the position and project, and will include intermittent clinical duty coverage (outpatient and-or inpatient) of other fellows or trainees absent due to leave or sickness. 
The position will allow protected time for clinical and-or translational research-audit that will focus on cancer-related projects agreed with the Head of Precision Medicine and-or Department Head, the Director of Research, under the day-to-day supervision of either the Director or another SVH-TKCC staff nominated by the Director. There will be an expectation of working towards specific KPIs such as publications, diplomas, degrees, intellectual property, and-or research data to support future grant applications. 

 

Where you'll be working

St Vincent's Health Network Sydney (SVHN) forms part of the NSW region of St Vincent's Health Australia which is the largest diversified health care organisation within Australia's not for profit and Catholic health care sectors. SVHN comprises some of Australia's oldest and most prestigious hospitals; these include St Vincent's Hospital and Sacred Heart Hospice. Along with three co-located research institutes - the Victor Chang Cardiac Research Institute, the Garvan Institute of Medical Research, and St Vincent's Institute of Medical Research - we work in close partnership with other research bodies, universities, and health care providers.

St. Vincents Hospital is a major public hospital and a principal tertiary referral hospital. St Vincents specialises in heart-lung transplantation; bone marrow transplantation; cardiology; neurosurgery, cancer; clinical genomics, HIV medicine; palliative care, respiratory medicine; mental health; and drug and alcohol services, aged psychiatry, homeless health and prisoner health. We are a clinical and education leader with a national and international reputation in medical research

Centrally located in Darlinghurst, it sits on the edge of Sydney's business district. St. Vincents follows the philosophy of the Mary Aikenhead Ministries in its service to all regardless of race, nationality or creed. St Vincent's Health Australia provides compassionate healthcare to people from all walks of life, but reflecting our mission, we are especially committed to people from vulnerable and marginalised backgrounds.

The Hospital has a long-standing reputation for treating the highest acuity and complex patient loads, attracting referrals on a state-wide and national basis. The Hospital is a teaching hospital of the UNSW and University of Notre Dame and has academic associations with the Australian Catholic University, Sydney University and the University of Technology, Sydney.

Interested in a new Senior Network Engineer opportunity?   
  Your new company  
 By joining the Queensland Government, you are joining a dynamic team committed to shaping and elevating Queensland's workforce to meet the evolving needs of our industries, ensuring prosperity and agility in our economic landscape. 
   
  Your new role   
 As a Senior Network Specialist within the Public Safety Network Centre (PSNMC) Deployment team, you will be crucial in the support of deploying network capabilities for the supported agencies. You will be responsible for configuring hardware for deployment, commission hardware for sites and the implementation of the project deliverables. 
   
  Key Responsibilities   
 As the Senior Network Specialist, you will: 
 
 
 Build and configure Cisco routers according to network specifications for operation within an SR-MPLS framework. 
 
 
 Update inventory and configuration records to reflect build of the devices. 
 
 
 Develop change documentation for subsequent approval by client agencies. 
 
 
 Commission routers and network monitoring hardware within the PSN remotely in conjunction with contracted installers on site. 
 
 
 Update inventory and configuration records to reflect commissioning of the new devices and removal of the previous devices. 
 
 
 Conduct data integrity checks for hardware and PSN sites. 
 
 
 Conduct handovers of hardware to the Operations team for ongoing support and maintenance. 
 
 
 Operate within PSNMC technical framework for Change, Release, Incident and Problem Management processes. 
 
 
   What you'll need to succeed  
 To thrive in this role, you will need to demonstrate the following: 
 
 
 Demonstrated experience with SR-MPLS networks. 
 
 
 Demonstrated understanding of overlay and underlay layer 3 routing protocols including MP-BGP and OSPF and experience in environments with hundreds of individual peering's using IPv4 and IPv6. 
 
 
 Demonstrated understanding of end to end Quality of Service (QoS) deployment regime incorporating: o MPLS QoS 
 
 
 o Layer 3 QoS in a non-MPLS environment 
 o Layer 2 QoS in a non-MPLS environment 
 
 
 Familiarity with Cisco routers. 
 
 
 Familiarity with Network Virtualisation Technologies e.g. MPLS VPNs including: VRFs, VPLS, EVPN, VRF-lite and VXLAN. 
 
 
 Demonstrated experience with wireless and radio networks, such as controller, access point, WLAN, 4/5G LTE design and deployment using Cisco. 
 
 
 Demonstrated experience managing authentication technologies such as TACACS, Radius, OTP, Active Directory, SAML / SSO and OAuth. 
 
 
 Demonstrated experience with remote access and encryption technologies for site to site (e.g. IPSEC VPNs, Cisco DMVPN) and client to site (e.g. SSL VPN) Always On VPN, and MACsec. 
 
 
 Demonstrated experience analysing packet captures and logs to determine application and network issues using tcpdump, Wireshark, NetScout and Splunk tools. 
 
 
 Demonstrated experience with carrier core, aggregation, access interconnect such as PNI, NNI and subscriber access. Retail and wholesale telecommunications service mapping and hand-off.

Westmead Hospital is a key facility of one of Australia's largest major health and medical research precincts and is the principal referral hospital for Western Sydney Local Health District providing district level health services to Parramatta, Holroyd and The Hills Shire LGAs including tertiary and quaternary services to greater Western Sydney, greater metropolitan Sydney, rural NSW and other states. It is a principal referral centre for other metropolitan hospitals within the district including Auburn Hospital, Blacktown and Mount Druitt Hospital.

Westmead Hospital is a leading centre of research, training and specialisation in all fields of Medicine and Dentistry, providing services in Cardiology, Cardiothoracic Surgery, Neurology, Neurosurgery, Kidney and Pancreas transplantation, Cancer Care, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Neonatal Intensive Care, Trauma, Bone Marrow Transplantation, Critical Care, Aged Care and Rehabilitation, Adult Acute Psychiatry (networked with the co-located Cumberland Hospital) as well as other specialised medical and surgical services.

The Westmead Hospital Emergency Department (ED) operates 24 hours, 7 days per week and manages all types and levels of illnesses and injuries. As one of six major trauma centres in the state, the ED also cares for people with the most severe physical injuries. Westmead Hospital ED presentation numbers are among the highest in the state, currently around 80,000 per year.

Westmead Hospital is one of Australia's largest centres for postgraduate training to specialist levels in all fields with over 100 PhD students and other postgraduate students supervised by Westmead Hospital scientists and clinicians. Westmead is home to internationally recognised institutes of health research, the most prominent being the Westmead Millennium Institute. The Westmead Millennium Institute is one of the largest medical research institutes in Australia, conducting research into a wide range of human disorders affecting both adults and children, including infectious and immune diseases, cancer and leukaemia, liver and metabolic diseases, eye and brain related disorders and heart and respiratory disorders.

Cumberland Hospital, co- located with Westmead Hospital provides primary and secondary mental health services to the local population and tertiary acute, extended and forensic mental health services to greater western Sydney and NSW. There is also a range of community mental health residential facilities, recovery support and specialist treatment services located on the campus.

The Trainee works as part of a multi-disciplinary team which includes medical, nursing and allied health professionals. They will work at the Senior resident medical officer (SRMO) level or Junior Registrar level (Depending on level of experience).

The Trainee is directly responsible to the supervising Emergency Medicine Specialist of the day, with overall supervision by the Term Supervisor and the Emergency Department Director.

The Trainee must work effectively with other specialty teams and nursing staff in the wider hospital, to ensure optimal patient care. The Trainee must also interact professionally with clinicians outside of the hospital, including GP's and community nurses.

What you'll be doing
WSLHD - Trainee Stage 1 - Emergency Medicine (Westmead) 
The primary purpose of the Trainee in the Emergency Department is to provide clinical care, under appropriate supervision, to patients requiring emergency medical services in a complex clinical environment. This position will provide experience in a critical care environment and have responsibilities and opportunities for autonomous practice commensurate with the level of experience of the incumbent.
The Trainee is expected to function at the minimum of a Senior Resident Medical Officer (SRMO) level.

The following rotations are available to Trainees:

. Other rotations may be negotiated depending on availability

It is expected that provisional trainees when eligible will apply to the Australasian College of Emergency Medicine (ACEM) for enrolment into training.

Westmead ED is accredited for provisional & advance training with 16 hours-7 days emergency physician cover.

Our teaching program has multiple streams dedicated to different requirements including a weekly registrar teaching. There are also skills days throughout the year specific for provisional trainees and preparation in both the primary and fellowship exam.

FerMax Stone Pty Ltd is an Australian company established in 2012, specialising in the installation of premium wall and floor tiling, natural stone, porcelain and other high-quality surface finishes for residential and commercial projects. Position Responsibilities and Tasks

As a Wall and Floor Tiler, your duties will include, but will not be limited to:

•	Interpret plans and specifications; confirm measurements, quantities, layout lines and levels prior to commencing tiling works.
•	Measure, mark and set out surfaces using levelling equipment (including laser levels) to establish correct alignment, falls and datum lines.
•	Measure, cut, shape and install custom heritage mosaic tiles and decorative stone finishes, ensuring accurate pattern alignment, preserving heritage design features and delivering high-quality workmanship in accordance with project specifications.
•	Prepare wall and floor substrates by removing old tiles, grout and adhesives; filling holes and cracks; and cleaning/priming surfaces to ensure suitable adhesion and finish.

•	Cut, shape and fit tiles using hand and power tile-cutting tools to finish edges, corners and penetrations around fittings, pipes and fixtures.
•	Maintain consistent alignment and spacing throughout installation, checking for lippage, level, line and falls, and adjusting as required during installation.
•	Complete grouting, finishing and clean-down, including removing excess grout and presenting a consistent, defect-free surface finish.
•	Support waterproofing outcomes by assisting with waterproofing preparation/detailing and coordinating tiling works with waterproofing stages and inspection hold points, ensuring correct detailing at junctions and penetrations in wet areas and external areas.
•	Undertake substrate preparation activities that support tiling quality (e.g., grinding, levelling and surface preparation), and coordinate transitions/interfaces with epoxy or other protective floor finishes where required by project scope.
•	Work collaboratively on major construction sites across Sydney/NSW, liaising with site foremen and project managers regarding sequencing, access, quality inspections and program timeframes.
•	Maintain compliance with WHS requirements, including safe manual handling, correct PPE use, silica dust controls and safe operation of plant and tools used for cutting and surface preparation.


Qualifications and Skills:

•	Certificate III in Wall and Floor Tiling or relevant trade qualification.
•	At least two years of relevant experience.
•	Sound knowledge of wall and floor tiling techniques and installation methods.
•	Experience working with ceramic, porcelain, marble, granite and natural stone products.
•	Ability to read and interpret plans and technical drawings.
•	Strong attention to detail and commitment to high-quality workmanship.

The role offers a remuneration package of $80,000 - $90,000 per annum, plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

About the Role






We are recruiting Implementation Specialist is a skilled and highly motivated implementation practitioner with experience in implementation science, systems thinking, quality improvement and health service transformation.






Working within the Monash Centre for Health Research and Implementation (MCHRI), the role will support the translation of evidence into practice through implementation support, capability building, mentoring, facilitation and applied implementation research.






The position will play a key role in the delivery of MCHRI's Implementation Science Academy, including co-facilitation of implementation science workshops, masterclasses and professional development programs. The role will support participants undertaking implementation projects through structured mentoring, coaching and practical implementation support.






The Implementation Specialist will work collaboratively with healthcare organisations, researchers, clinicians, consumers and system leaders to apply implementation science and systems approaches to complex healthcare challenges. This includes supporting implementation planning, barrier and enabler assessments, strategy selection, evaluation design, and sustainability planning.






The role will also contribute to implementation research, grant development, scholarly outputs and the advancement of Learning Health Systems and implementation science capability across healthcare settings. 






Strong facilitation, stakeholder engagement, communication, analytical and problem-solving skills are essential for success in this role.

MCHRI sits under the Facility of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences at Monash University. Established in 2005, MCHRI has grown from 3 to 180 staff and students. This is a partnership centre across Monash University and Monash Health and provides an implementation laboratory for research and translation embedded and integrated into healthcare. MCHRI works with broader reach across Monash Partners Academic Health Science Centre, nationally and internationally in our research and translation endeavours. Our vision is to create, synthesise, implement and translate clinical, health care and public health knowledge, underpinned by cross sector end user engagement, to deliver health impact. MCHRI has led organisational and individual leadership support programs in healthcare for nearly a decade.

Co-facilitate implementation science masterclasses, workshops and capability-building programs delivered through MCHRI.

About You:







Degree qualification in a relevant discipline and demonstrated experience in healthcare, health services, healthcare improvement, implementation, policy, research translation or related sectors.   Demonstrated ability to leverage modern AI tools to efficiently resolve day to day technical accounting challenges.

The Workplace AI Product Owner is responsible for the end-to-end ownership of Anglicare's workplace AI product ecosystem. Operating within Digital and AI Enablement group of products, this role has organisation-wide reach and manages a growing portfolio of workplace AI capabilities, adoption pathways, enablement assets, governance processes, and approved automation scenarios that improve productivity, decision support, and staff effectiveness.

With ownership, you will manage the following:

Product Ownership and Delivery

Enable approved automation and agent scenarios that extend Workplace AI outcomes, while working within enterprise guardrails and partnering with business owners for implementation and operational support.

Build strong relationships across leadership, business, and technology teams to align stakeholders around priorities, investment choices, and responsible adoption.

Benefits Realisation and Insights

Define, measure, and report on Workplace AI product KPIs, adoption indicators, and benefit outcomes across personas and use cases.

Quantify how Workplace AI initiatives contribute to business outcomes such as time savings, improved quality, reduced cycle time, stronger decision support, and workforce effectiveness.

Use data, feedback, and experimentation to validate opportunities, inform prioritisation, and guide future investment decisions.

You will be equipped with the following skills.

Gen AI, automation or digital transformation initiatives

Product management (Agile, discovery-delivery)

Change management

Stakeholder engagement and communication

Technical fluency and systems thinking

Benefits realisation and performance measurement

Bachelor's degree in digital, technology, business, or a related field.

5+ years experience in product management, digital workplace, or a related role; or 1-2 years experience in gen AI enablement

Experience leading adoption, change, enablement, or capability uplift initiatives across diverse user groups.

Hands-on experience with Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Anthropic Claude

The Monash Health Cybersecurity team helps enable safe, resilient and trusted care by protecting the digital systems, information and technologies that support clinical care and business operations. As Monash Health continues to expand its digital capability, connectivity and innovation, the Cybersecurity team plays a critical role in reducing cyber risk, strengthening organisational resilience, and supporting the safe and reliable delivery of services across the organisation.


The Cybersecurity team is responsible for protecting Monash Health's digital environment, including clinical systems, medical devices, enterprise applications, patient information, workforce technologies and supporting infrastructure. The team works in partnership with stakeholders across the Digital and Information Division and the broader organisation to identify, assess and manage cyber risk, support secure service delivery, and improve cyber maturity and technology resilience.

Strong working knowledge of contemporary cyber security frameworks and standards, including ISO 27001, ISO 31000, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, the Australian Government Information Security Manual (ISM) and the Essential Eight.


Sound knowledge of legislative, regulatory and policy obligations relevant to Victorian public health services, including the Privacy and Data Protection Act 2014 (Vic), Health Records Act 2001 (Vic), and the Security of Critical Infrastructure (SOCI) framework.


Demonstrated ability to think strategically and systematically, identify emerging issues, manage competing priorities and support risk-based decision-making in a complex service delivery environment.
